name: Claude Code
runs_on: Anthropic's Claude models (Opus, Sonnet, Haiku and others)
can_act_on: Files, terminal and shell, code execution, GitHub and GitLab, other tools via MCP connectors
access: Paid Claude plans (Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise) and API accounts
security_evidence: Asks permission before changing files or running commands; an automatic mode on most paid plans lets it work longer while still stopping risky commands. Runs locally and calls the model API directly. In October 2026 Noma Security disclosed SneakPeek, a Claude Code Desktop preview pane flaw (CVSS 8.7) that could leak SSH keys and tokens from a poisoned file; Anthropic fixed it. Also in October 2026, Anthropic fixed a High-rated plugin pin bypass (CVE-2026-86063) that could install attacker-controlled plugin code, in version 2.1.179.

name: Claude in Chrome
can_act_on: Web browsing using your own logins: reads pages, clicks, types and fills in forms across tabs
access: All paid Claude plans since 26 Aug 2026; admins can limit it to approved sites
security_evidence: Anthropic reports prompt-injection attacks succeeded 3.8% of the time against Opus 5 before extra safeguards, and none against Sonnet 5, Opus 5 or Mythos 5 with its probes and action classifier (0.3% for Fable 5). These are Anthropic's own figures.

name: OpenAI Codex
maker_note: Desktop app merged into the ChatGPT desktop app in July 2026.
runs_on: OpenAI's GPT models (GPT-6.1 Sol in Codex; GPT-5.5-Cyber for Codex Security)
open_source: Partly (the command-line tool is open source; the app is not)
can_act_on: Files, terminal and shell, code execution in a sandbox, optional internet access, GitHub
security_evidence: In March 2026 researchers found a now-patched flaw where malicious GitHub branch names could inject commands and retrieve GitHub tokens. In October 2026 Codex CLI 0.163.0 tightened network proxy and sandbox controls and turned on cyber access programmes by default for API-key sessions.

name: ChatGPT agent
maker_note: Replaced Operator, which closed on 31 Aug 2025.
runs_on: OpenAI models, starting with its Computer-Using Agent model
can_act_on: Web browsing on its own virtual computer, research, forms, bookings and orders
security_evidence: Asks for confirmation before significant actions, and the user can stop a task at any time.

name: Gemini agent
maker_note: Launched 8 Oct 2026, for businesses first; consumers later.
runs_on: Picks a model per task; users can also choose, including Anthropic's Claude models
can_act_on: Email and its own Workspace account, documents, Microsoft 365, Slack, Jira, code repositories, databases, any MCP server
security_evidence: Keeps an audit trail attributed to the agent rather than a person. Google has not published security detail beyond that.

name: Microsoft 365 Copilot (incl. Researcher, Copilot Cowork, Copilot Studio agents)
runs_on: OpenAI's GPT models and Anthropic's Claude models; Researcher uses both, Copilot Cowork runs on Claude
can_act_on: Email, documents, Teams, SharePoint and other Microsoft 365 data; other systems via connectors
access: Microsoft 365 Copilot licences; agent features depend on licence and admin settings

name: GitHub Copilot coding agent
runs_on: A choice of models depending on plan, including premium third-party models
can_act_on: Files, code execution and tests in a temporary cloud environment, one GitHub repository and branch per task; opens pull requests
security_evidence: Sessions last at most 59 minutes and touch one repository; repository rules can block it and owners can switch it off per repository.

name: OpenClaw
maker_note: Formerly Clawdbot and Moltbot. Its creator, Peter Steinberger, joined OpenAI in Feb 2026; the project moved to a foundation and stays open source.
runs_on: Any: Claude, GPT, Gemini, open-weight models such as DeepSeek, Kimi and Qwen, or local models
can_act_on: Terminal and shell, files, code execution, web browsing, WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack, Teams, Signal and other messaging apps; add-on 'skills' from a public registry
access: Free; self-hosted on your own machine or server
security_evidence: CVE-2026-25253 (CVSS 8.8) let a malicious website hijack the assistant and was exploited in the wild; in late Jan 2026 at least 14 malicious skills were uploaded to its public registry; over 1,800 exposed instances leaked API keys and chat histories.

name: Cursor
maker_note: SpaceX completed its $60bn purchase on 14 Aug 2026. SpaceX also owns xAI.
runs_on: A choice of models from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, xAI and Meta, plus Cursor's own Composer
can_act_on: Files, terminal and shell, code execution, other tools via MCP

name: Devin
maker_note: Cognition also owns the Windsurf editor, run as a separate product.
runs_on: Not confirmed: Cognition does not name the models publicly
can_act_on: Its own cloud machine with browser, terminal and editor; GitHub, GitLab, Jira, Linear, Slack, Sentry
access: Paid plans from $20 a month; enterprise options include data residency

name: Manus
maker_note: Meta bought Manus (reported at over $2bn), announced 31 Dec 2025, and still sells it.
can_act_on: Web browsing, research and multi-step tasks

name: Dots
maker_note: Launched at DevDay on 29 Sep 2026; one Dot per user at launch.
can_act_on: Always on: uses a computer and connected apps to research, draft documents and write software; reached through ChatGPT, Slack or Microsoft Teams
access: ChatGPT Pro and Business Premium first; beta for Enterprise, Edu and Healthcare, off unless an admin enables it
security_evidence: Users set boundaries on what a Dot may do on its own; admins control whether it is enabled. OpenAI has published no further security detail.

name: Meta AI (agent features)
maker_note: Agent features rolled out from late July 2026, in selected countries first; WhatsApp to follow.
runs_on: Meta's Muse Spark models (Muse Spark 1.1 at launch)
can_act_on: Your email and calendar, the web, Facebook Marketplace shopping, recurring tasks run without you, documents and slides
access: Public, through the Meta AI app and meta.ai in selected countries
security_evidence: Meta has not detailed how it retains data or controls permissions for email and calendar access. Users can switch to Incognito chats instead.

name: Muse Code
maker_note: Launched in beta on 5 August 2026 running Muse Spark 1.2. Since 12 October 2026 it also offers Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full.
can_act_on: Code repositories and the developer's terminal

name: Cairn
maker_note: Published on GitHub by a developer known as le1xia0; NorForge reports the author said it was not designed for hacking.
runs_on: Not confirmed; NorForge saw workers named for Claude Code and the Pi agent driven by DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, including via OpenRouter
can_act_on: Coordinates multiple AI agents against a target, sharing discovered facts and planned steps; used for penetration testing
access: Free; self-hosted with a web control panel
security_evidence: NorForge found more than 20 exposed Cairn control panels in malicious use by three groups, attempting intrusions on over 1,200 websites; the panels leaked hundreds of secrets.

name: OpenCode
runs_on: Multiple AI providers through user-linked API keys
can_act_on: Terminal and shell, files and code; connects to MCP servers
access: Free to install; OpenCode Console hosted workspaces
security_evidence: In October 2026 a breach exposed AI provider API keys linked by 1.4% of OpenCode Console users. Pillar Security also reported a remote code execution flaw (CVSS 9.8) in which a malicious MCP server could run code on Windows or WSL during OAuth sign-in; fixed in 1.18.33 without a CVE.
